states.narration: The same product xy occurs twice, multiplied by two and by four. Keep that product intact.
Collect the shared product on the left. The two original multipliers form the sum on the right.
Evaluate two plus four as six. The product xy and its position on the left remain unchanged.

editorial.title: Collect a shared product on the left
editorial.setup: Treat xy as one unit while combining its multipliers.
editorial.summary: Factoring keeps the shared product intact; evaluation simplifies only its multiplier. No division occurs, so either x or y may be zero.
